Text: Bankers have told potential investors the Anthropic could target a valuation exceeding $2T (more than double its ~$965B private mark from the May Series H) & potentially raise more than $100B, which would make it the largest IPO on record & surpass SpaceX’s earlier 2026 debut. $MS is positioned for the lead-left role, w/ $GS as co-lead. JPMorgan & Citigroup are also in the top tier of the syndicate The newly detailed prospectus shows rapid top-line growth alongside heavy investment: • Revs: $4.59B, up +1,088% y/y from $386M • Op loss: $8.06B, widening from $2.98B in 2024. • GAAP net loss: $41.97B, vs $8.31B the prior year. That headline ~$42B net loss requires context- roughly $34B stemmed from an accounting charge tied largely to the rising value of financing instruments that could eventually convert into Anthropic shares, rather than cash spent running the business Anthropic spent $7.33B on compute & infrastructure in 2025—up +190% y/y & nearly 3x the prior year. That alone represented: • 58% of its $12.65B in total op expenses • Roughly 1.6x its entire annual revs Spending is expected to keep climbing. The prospectus outlines roughly $518B in cloud, compute & infrastructure obligations as the company continues building out its AI systems. Anthropic ended 2025 w/ $20.28B in total cash Its 2 largest direct customers each acct’d for 12% of revs, meaning just 2 customers represented 24% of total 2025 sales Anthropic warns that many of its largest customers are not locked into long-term contracts & could reduce or stop spending $AMZN & $GOOGL are also major strategic partners & investors in Anthropic, while supplying much of the cloud infrastructure needed to train & run Claude The IPO could come after the Nov US midterm elections & would give public-market investors one of their 1st pure-play ways to value a frontier AI lab The filing highlights risks around increasingly autonomous AI systems, including unexpected behavior, security concerns & potential misuse

Text: Google has been paying about 100 digital publishers for content used in AI-powered answers across its search engine and other products, The Information reported Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter. The pilot program marks a shift from Google’s traditional position that it should not pay publishers whose content helps answer user queries, arguing that search traffic directs users to their websites and provides economic value. However, the rollout of AI-generated summaries, known as AI Overviews, has significantly reduced the amount of traffic Google sends to publishers’ sites. The change has triggered widespread complaints and lawsuits from some publishers, who argue that Google is benefiting from their content while reducing the traffic that supports their businesses. Under the proposed structure, thousands of Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips deployed across more than a dozen U.S. data centers would be transferred to a special-purpose vehicle funded by outside investors. Amazon would then lease the hardware back, allowing it to continue using the chips while reducing the amount of AI infrastructure held directly on its balance sheet. The special-purpose entity could issue debt and potentially sell up to 10% of its equity to investors. Meanwhile, Samsung has raised prices on most Galaxy S26 models by $100, while Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max also launched above their predecessors’ prices. Google’s newer Pixel 11 lineup started at $899, $100 above the previous generation, with the company adding more storage to entry-level configurations to offset part of the increase. Text: Google successfully launched its prototype Project Suncatcher satellite into space aboard SpaceX’s Transporter-18 rideshare mission, confirming that contact has been established and the satellite is operating as expected. Author: topstockalerts
Text: Google’s Quantum AI team demonstrated a technique called “magic state cultivation” that reduced errors approximately 40-fold on its Willow quantum processor, according to research published Thursday in Science. The breakthrough addresses a major bottleneck in quantum computing: producing reliable magic states, which are essential for executing complex quantum programs and could consume up to 95% of a quantum computer’s processing capacity. Google’s approach uses coordinated measurements to identify errors and filter out unsuccessful attempts, generating higher-quality quantum states with fewer resources. On Willow, the technique achieved 99.99% logical fidelity for T states, a type of magic state required for universal quantum computing. Researchers also demonstrated that these cultivated states could be transferred between two quantum error-correction methods, potentially enabling integration into Google’s existing architecture. $GOOGL
